title: SOP For Disposal of Filled Blood Tubes & Container by Autoclaving
html:
SOP For Disposal of Filled Blood Tubes & Container by Autoclaving

  • Purpose

This procedure covers safe disposal of blood tubes & containers by treatment with autoclaving.

  • Scope

Blood tubes & container are used for collecting blood sample in laboratory. Once used for processing required test the blood tubes & containers will need to be treated prior to disposal to reduce any potential for infection.

  • Responsibilities
  • Appropriate PPE. When handling blood or blood products, always use:
    • Eye protection (safety glasses or goggles) to protect against blood splatter.
    • A mask to prevent breathing air-borne pathogens.
    • Gloves to protect your skin from spills or leaks.
    • Laboratory coat or other protective clothing to protect your upper body from spillages.
    • Closed shoes.
  • Hazards and Safety Concerns
    • Always
      • Wear appropriate PPE.
      • Wash your hands with soap after handling blood or blood products.
  • Procedures
    • Preparing for treatment
      • For blood tubes & containers with contaminated contents or those considered potentially infectious, ensure all the liquid and the containers are sent for autoclaving to disinfect them prior to disposal.
    • Loading the blood tubes & containers in the autoclave
      • Load the blood tubes & containers in single layers to ensure the steam is able to heat the liquids effectively.
        • Undertake a full validation for this waste stream to determine the correct parameters required for disinfection of the blood tubes & containers.
        • Some of the modifications likely in a successful blood tubes & containers cycle include:
        • It can be anticipated that each load of filled blood tubes & containers may need at least another 20 minutes at 121°C to ensure effective disinfection. Some researchers recommend 1 hour’s autoclaving.
        • Use a liquid cycle because the longer cooling down period will allow more time for the blood tubes & containers to be effectively disinfected and minimize boiling of liquids due to rapid pressure drops.
        • Do not vent for at least 20 minutes after the usual disinfection time has elapsed.
  • Reporting and Recordkeeping
    • The number or mass of blood tubes & containers autoclaved should be included in the autoclave operation log.
    • Report any incidents or accidents, such as spills and needle stick injuries, according to standard institutional procedures. Where the relevant authorities prescribed must be notified of any incidents, such as needle stick injuries.
